description:
Fill the scaffold stubs in pkix-identity created by PKIX-fmtv.21 with the RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6 + RFC 8398 mailbox binding implementation. Scope is the pkix-identity half ONLY; pkix-chain verify_smime_signer/verify_smime_recipient wrappers are split out as PKIX-fmtv.12.2 (blocked on PKIX-fmtv.7's wrapper-set decision, which is human-labeled).

## Deliverable

### pkix-identity changes

Add workspace deps used by this body:
- `idna` 1.x (workspace, no_std with `alloc` feature; std opt-in via crate feature)
- `der` (already a workspace dep; may need extra features for extension parsing)

Implement `MailboxName::parse(mailbox: &'a str) -> Result<Self, IdentityError>`:
- Validate against RFC 5322 mailbox syntax (local-part "@" domain, basic checks).
- Support RFC 8398 internationalized mailbox (UTF-8 local-part allowed).
- Store local-part and domain split (private fields).

Implement `verify_mailbox(cert: &Certificate, mailbox: &MailboxName) -> Result<(), IdentityError>`:
- Parse leaf's SubjectAlternativeName extension (OID 2.5.29.17); iterate `GeneralName` entries.
- For each `GeneralName::Rfc822Name(addr)`:
  - Local-part: case-sensitive byte compare (per RFC 5321 §2.4 — local-part case sensitivity is left to receiving domain; we choose case-sensitive for safety, matches webpki + pyca behaviour).
  - Domain part: case-insensitive ASCII compare (per RFC 1035 / RFC 5321).
- For each `GeneralName::OtherName { type_id: id-on-SmtpUTF8Mailbox (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.9), value }`:
  - Decode `value` as UTF-8 mailbox per RFC 8398 §3.
  - Same case rules but on UTF-8 (NOT folding non-ASCII local-part).
  - Domain: U-label → A-label via `idna` crate before compare.
- If any matches: `Ok(())`.
- If SAN present but no entry matches: `Err(IdentityError::NoMatchingSan)`.
- If SAN missing: `Err(IdentityError::MissingSan)`.

Add new `IdentityError` variant if needed (the bead body uses `NoMatchingMailbox` — see if `NoMatchingSan` from the scaffold is reusable or if a more specific variant is wanted).

## Test fixtures

Need leaf certs with:
1. `rfc822Name=alice@example.com` SAN (single ASCII rfc822Name).
2. `rfc822Name=alice@example.com` SAN (test domain-case mismatch: `alice@Example.com`).
3. `otherName` with `id-on-SmtpUTF8Mailbox` containing `用户@example.com` (internationalized local-part).
4. SAN with BOTH rfc822Name (ASCII) and otherName (UTF-8) variants.
5. Cert without SAN (negative test for `MissingSan`).

Generation oracle: OpenSSL (`openssl req -x509 -addext 'subjectAltName=email:...'` for rfc822Name) + pyca/cryptography for the SmtpUTF8Mailbox otherName variant (openssl does not support otherName naturally; pyca's UnstructuredName / OtherName types do).

## Tests

Mirror the bead body's 5 test scenarios:
- Plain ASCII match.
- Local-part case sensitivity: `Alice@example.com` vs SAN `alice@example.com` → reject.
- Domain case insensitivity: `alice@Example.com` vs SAN `alice@example.com` → accept.
- RFC 8398 otherName match: input `用户@example.com` vs SAN otherName UTF-8 → accept.
- Mixed SAN: cert with both rfc822Name and otherName; verify both code paths.
- SAN missing → `MissingSan`.
- SAN present but no entry matches → `NoMatchingSan`.

Independent oracles: pyca/cryptography's `certificate.extensions.get_extension_for_class(x509.SubjectAlternativeName)` + `san.get_values_for_type(x509.RFC822Name)` + `san.get_values_for_type(x509.OtherName)` for cross-validation.

## Out of scope (split to PKIX-fmtv.12.2)

- `pkix_chain::verify_smime_signer`/`verify_smime_recipient` wrappers — depend on PKIX-fmtv.7 (human-labeled, wrapper-set decision).
- New `VerifyError` variants in pkix-chain.

## Acceptance

- `cargo build -p pkix-identity` clean (default features + `--no-default-features`).
- `cargo build -p pkix-identity --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` clean (no_std preserved).
- `cargo clippy -p pkix-identity --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean.
- All 7 test scenarios pass.
- CHANGELOG entry in `pkix-identity/CHANGELOG.md` and top-level CHANGELOG for the body landing.

## What this unblocks

PKIX-fmtv.12.2 (pkix-chain S/MIME wrappers, still blocked on .7) and any future pkix-chain caller that wants mailbox binding without the wrapper convenience.
title: Implement RFC 5280/8398 mailbox binding body in pkix-identity (verify_mailbox + MailboxName::parse)
